title: Don’t get one-shotted: Use AI to test, review, merge, and deploy code — Tomas Reimers, Graphite

summary: Tomas Reimers, co-founder of Graphite (an AI code review company), frames software development as having two loops: the inner loop focused on development and the outer loop focused on review, testing, merging, and deployment. AI tools like Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, v0, and Bolt are dramatically accelerating the inner loop, with nearly every developer surveyed using AI tools and 46% of GitHub code written by Copilot. This increased code volume is making the outer loop the primary bottleneck. Reimers explains that problems once unique to large companies—high volumes of code changes requiring review, testing, and deployment—now affect all companies. The new outer loop requires tools for prioritizing and tracking pull requests, driver-assist features for reviewers, optimized CI pipelines and merge queues, and better deployment tools. Graphite's approach applies AI to solve problems AI creates. Reimers notes that AI-generated feedback isn't perfect—AI can hallucinate, make mistakes, and introduce security vulnerabilities. Simply adding AI teammates or background agents is insufficient; the entire tool chain must be AI-native, not just the IDE. Graphite built Diamond, an AI code review platform with high signal and low noise, deep understanding of the codebase and change history. Diamond summarizes, prioritizes, and reviews each change, integrating with CI and testing infrastructure to summarize errors and correct failures. It offers zero setup, one-click actionable suggestions, and customization while keeping code private and secure. By the numbers, Diamond's AI comments are dismissed at less than 4% and accepted into pull requests at approximately 52%, exceeding human comment acceptance rates of 45–50%. Reimers encourages embracing AI across the entire developer workflow to handle the volume of AI-assisted code.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and the Two Loops of Software Development
sections.summary: Tomas Reimers introduces himself as co-founder of Graphite, an AI code review company. He frames software development as having two loops: the inner loop focused on development and the outer loop focused on review, testing, merging, and deployment.

sections.title: AI Transforming the Inner Loop
sections.summary: Reimers presents statistics showing nearly universal AI tool adoption among developers and 46% of GitHub code written by Copilot. The inner loop is changing more than ever, with developers producing higher volumes of code, but that code still needs review.

sections.title: The Outer Loop Becoming the Bottleneck
sections.summary: AI can hallucinate, make mistakes, and introduce security vulnerabilities. While the inner loop speeds up, the outer loop becomes the bottleneck. Problems once limited to large companies now affect all companies dealing with higher code volumes. The new outer loop requires tools for PR prioritization, reviewer assist features, optimized CI pipelines, merge queues, and better deployment tools.

sections.title: Toward an AI-Native Outer Loop
sections.summary: Reimers argues that problems created by AI can be solved by AI. However, AI-generated feedback isn't perfect, and simply adding AI teammates or background agents isn't enough. The entire tool chain must be AI-native, not just the IDE, to handle orders-of-magnitude productivity gains.

sections.title: Diamond: AI Code Review Platform and Results
sections.summary: Graphite built Diamond, an AI code review platform with high signal, low noise, deep codebase understanding, zero setup, one-click suggestions, and CI/testing integration. Diamond comments are dismissed at less than 4% and accepted at ~52%, exceeding human comment acceptance of 45–50%. Reimers encourages embracing AI across the entire developer workflow.
